rules.title: Security deposit capped at one month's rent (AB 12)
rules.requirement: Since July 1, 2024, most landlords may charge no more than one month's rent as a security deposit, whether the unit is furnished or unfurnished. Last month's rent counts toward this limit; first month's rent does not.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental tenancies in California starting on or after July 1, 2024, furnished or unfurnished.
rules.exemptions: A landlord that is a natural person, family trust, or LLC whose members are all natural persons, and that owns no more than two rental properties with no more than four residential units total, may charge up to two months' rent.
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

exemption_tests.description: Small landlord (natural person, family trust, or LLC with all natural-person members) owning only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total may charge up to two months' rent.

rules.title: Return of deposit within 21 days with itemized statement and receipts
rules.requirement: The landlord must return the deposit, or whatever is left of it, within 21 days after the tenant moves out. If anything is deducted, the landlord must give an itemized statement with copies of bills, invoices or receipts. Since January 1, 2025, the landlord must also show proof that the repairs were done.
rules.quoted_span:
All or any remaining portion of a security deposit must be returned
within 21 days
after the tenant/s leave the unit vacant.

rules.title: Photo documentation at move-in and before deduction repairs
rules.requirement: For tenancies starting on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit right before or at the start of the tenancy. Since April 1, 2025, the landlord must also photograph the unit after getting it back but before any repairs or cleaning it plans to deduct for, and must give the tenant those photos with the itemized statement.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in California; the move-in photo rule applies to tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.
rules.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 (as amended by AB 2801 (2024))
rules.quoted_span: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of a unit after regaining possession, but before any repairs or cleaning for which the landlord intends to make a deduction from the security deposit.
rules.conflict_note: This one record covers two effective dates: April 1, 2025 for move-out/pre-repair photos and July 1, 2025 for move-in photos.

rules.title: Limits on deposit deductions
rules.requirement: A landlord may deduct only what is reasonably necessary for unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear and tear, cleaning back to move-in condition, and, if the lease allows, replacing personal property or keys. The landlord cannot charge for professional carpet cleaning or other professional cleaning unless it is reasonably necessary.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot require a tenant to pay for, or assert a claim against the tenant or the security deposit for professional carpet cleaning or other professional cleaning services, unless reasonably necessary to return the premises to the condition it was in at the start of the tenancy, minus ordinary wear and tear.

rules.title: Pre-move-out walk-through inspection
rules.requirement: The landlord must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of the tenancy so the tenant can fix problems and avoid deductions. Tenants should ask for one if the landlord doesn't offer it.
rules.quoted_span: Under state law, landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy to identify any items that need repair/cleaning.

rules.title: Annual interest on security deposits
rules.requirement: If your unit is fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, the landlord must pay you interest on your security deposit at the end of each year, plus a prorated amount if you move out partway through the year.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance (B.M.C. Ch. 13.76)
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

unresolvable_conditions: whether the unit is fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance (the coverage tests are not stated in this document)

notes: The document only cites 'Assembly Bill 12' and 'state law'. The Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 citation and AB 2801 for the photo rules come from outside knowledge, not from this document. The page doesn't give the ordinance section, interest rate or coverage tests for Berkeley's deposit interest rule; it points to a separate Security Deposit Interest & Calculator page.
